```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
```


```{r}
library(maps)
```

read data/breeding_site_locations.csv into a variable, then view it with gt

```{r}
bird_breeding_sites <- read_csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
gt(bird_breeding_sites)
```

We can view just the column names from the data frame using the function colnames().
```{r}
colnames(bird_breeding_sites)
```

We can use the function glimpse() to see a summary of the data frame
```{r}
glimpse(bird_breeding_sites)
```
At the top is then a summary of each column. The second column shows <chr> or <dbl> - <chr> columns contain character data and <dbl> columns contain numeric data (R calls some types of numeric data double)


use nrow() to see just the number of rows
ncol() to see just the number of columns
dim() to see both (the dimensions)
```{r}
print(nrow(bird_breeding_sites))
print(ncol(bird_breeding_sites))
print(dim(bird_breeding_sites))
```

```{r}
migration_dataset <- read_csv("data/migratory_connectivity_dataset.csv")
gt(head(migration_dataset))
```

to select certain columns for the data set, we can do this
```{r}
bird_breeding_selected <- bird_breeding_sites |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |>
#use the distinct() function to eliminate the duplicated rows
  distinct() |>
  rename(Breeding_Longitude = Longitude, Breeding_Latitude = Latitude)


gt(bird_breeding_selected)
```

```{r}
bird_migration_sites_selected <- migration_dataset |>
  select(Site, 
         winterLongitude, 
         winterLatitude, 
         pslon, 
         pslat, 
         iblon, 
         iblat, 
         awestlon, 
         awestlat) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Winter_Longitude = winterLongitude, 
         Winter_Latitude = winterLatitude, 
         Stopover_Longitude = pslon, 
         Stopover_Latitude = pslat, 
         Iberian_Longitude = iblon, 
         Iberian_Latitude = iblat, 
         Westmost_Longitude = awestlon, 
         Westmost_Latitude = awestlat)

gt(bird_migration_sites_selected)
```

On our data frame columns, we can use the function filter() to get the rows which match our criteria.
```{r}
bird_breeding_dartmoor <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Site == "Dartmoor")

gt(bird_breeding_dartmoor)

#To get rows for everywhere except Dartmoor:

bird_breeding_not_dartmoor <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Site != "Dartmoor")

gt(bird_breeding_not_dartmoor)

#To get rows where Breeding_Longitude is greater than 10:

bird_breeding_long_10 <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Breeding_Longitude > 10)

gt(bird_breeding_long_10)
```

exclude breeding site data and migration site data from Spain
```{r}
bird_breeding_exc <- bird_breeding_selected |>
  filter(Site != "Spain")

gt(bird_breeding_exc)

# now from the bird migration site
bird_migration_exc <- bird_migration_sites_selected |>
  filter(Site != "Spain")

gt(bird_breeding_exc)
```
